E3 stale-frame replay rejection. Firmware hook: session_send.c stage_tx_esl_wrap emits the previously saved ESL-wrapped blob verbatim when armed (task_session.c arming at s_bench_sent%10==4), so the injected frame carries a stale ESL header at least 5s old while a fresh ARQ seq is applied downstream, which prevents link-layer duplicate suppression from confounding the crypto replay defence (the E2b confound). Expect about 8 injections and 8 forges per 80-frame campaign. DISCLOSED CAVEATS: (1) Toolchain is ESP-IDF v6.0.2 (C:\esp\v6.0.2\esp-idf, tag v6.0.2), the same version that built E1/E2a/E2b/E5. An earlier draft of this manifest claimed v6.0.3 and asserted that v6.0.2 had been deleted from the machine and could not be restored; that assertion was wrong and is corrected in PREREGISTRATION.md section 8. A build of this exact configuration on v6.0.3 was attempted and failed at link with 'region dram0_0_seg overflowed by 16 bytes', which is why it was abandoned. Compiler identical (xtensa-esp-elf 15.2.0_20251204). This run's generated sdkconfig.h is byte-identical to build_cap_ceepew's, the Mode C capture configuration used for E1-C/E2a/E2b. (2) CONFIG_CEEPEW_BENCH_TIMING is OFF (DRAM pressure at link time), so no BENCH_TIME records exist for this run and no latency claim may be derived from it. (3) Hopping off, channel 1, as pre-registered.

E5 sync-pulse latency. Both boards pulse AND sense on shared GPIO14 (D14-D14 open-drain jumper). All intervals are SAME-CLOCK only; no cross-board subtraction is performed anywhere. BENCH58: 80 frames/board at 5s spacing. 300 BENCH_TIME records recovered (160 tx, 140 rx).
